phrases.text: The people of Mecca had offered the Prophet a bargain: they would worship God for a year if he would worship their gods for a year. God tells him what to say in answer.
The address is to certain people of the polytheists whom God knew would never believe, so that the Prophet would take from them the hope they had built on this bargain.

phrases.translation: I do not worship what you worship
phrases.text: The gods and the idols, at this present moment.
Tabari sets the whole shape of the answer out: not now, and not in the future, on either side. Some of them were killed at Badr and the rest died as disbelievers.

phrases.translation: nor do you worship what I worship
phrases.text: The same bargain, answered the other way round, at this present moment.
And in the future, never. The whole address is a closing of the door on any hope that this bargain might come about.

phrases.translation: I will never worship what you worship
phrases.text: What you worshipped in the past. Tabari sets the whole answer out word by word, past and present and future on both sides.
And the reports agree: the offer was made twice, first with wealth and marriage and then with the year of worship, and both were refused with the same words.

phrases.translation: nor will you ever worship what I worship
phrases.text: Never, in the future, what I worship now and what I shall worship then.
Tabari repeats the reason: God knew they would never believe, so the answer is given to leave them nothing to hope for.

phrases.translation: You have your way, and I have my Way.
phrases.text: Your religion you will never leave, for it is sealed for you and you will die upon it. And my religion is the one I stand on, and I will never turn from it.
Tabari notes that the repetition through the surah is emphasis, the way God repeats His words about ease after hardship.
